messages.content: I need to log into my account.

function.name: user_authentication_authenticate
function.description: Authenticate a user based on their username and password. Returns a session token if successful. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

username.description: The username of the user attempting to authenticate.

password.description: The password for the user attempting to authenticate.

remember_me.description: Whether to keep the user logged in across sessions.

login_attempts.description: The number of unsuccessful login attempts before this one. If it reaches a certain threshold, additional verification may be required.

message.content: Sure! To get started, could you please provide your username and password? (Feel free to type them in a private or secure channel if you prefer.)
message.reasoning: The user wants to log into their account. We have a tool function for authentication. We should call the function with the username and password. But we don't have the credentials. We need to ask the user for them. According to policy, we should not store or reveal them. We can ask for username and password. We should not store them. We can call the function after receiving them. So we should ask for username and password.
